---
title: "Events in C#"
---

Events build directly on delegates. Now that you understand delegates, events will make a lot of sense!


## Why Events? (The Problem with Plain Delegates)

With plain delegates, any code can **invoke** or **overwrite** the delegate:

```csharp
// Using plain delegate (problematic)
class Button
{
    public Action? OnClick;  // Anyone can access this!
}

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var button = new Button();
        button.OnClick = () => Console.WriteLine("Clicked!");
        
        // PROBLEM 1: External code can OVERWRITE all subscribers
        button.OnClick = () => Console.WriteLine("I replaced everyone!");
        
        // PROBLEM 2: External code can INVOKE the delegate directly
        button.OnClick?.Invoke();  // Fake click from outside!
    }
}
```

**Events** solve this by adding restrictions:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  DELEGATE vs EVENT                                                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  Plain Delegate:                                                    │
│    ✅ Subscribe:   obj.OnClick += Handler;                          │
│    ✅ Unsubscribe: obj.OnClick -= Handler;                          │
│    ⚠️ Overwrite:   obj.OnClick = Handler;     ← Can replace all!    │
│    ⚠️ Invoke:      obj.OnClick();             ← Can trigger from    │
│                                                  outside!           │
│                                                                     │
│  Event:                                                             │
│    ✅ Subscribe:   obj.OnClick += Handler;                          │
│    ✅ Unsubscribe: obj.OnClick -= Handler;                          │
│    ❌ Overwrite:   obj.OnClick = Handler;     ← Compile error!      │
│    ❌ Invoke:      obj.OnClick();             ← Compile error!      │
│                                                  (only owner can)   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Publisher/Subscriber Pattern

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PUBLISHER / SUBSCRIBER PATTERN                                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│                      ┌─────────────────┐                            │
│                      │   PUBLISHER     │                            │
│                      │   (Event Owner) │                            │
│                      │                 │                            │
│                      │  - Defines event│                            │
│                      │  - Raises event │                            │
│                      └────────┬────────┘                            │
│                               │                                     │
│                          event fires                                │
│                               │                                     │
│              ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐                    │
│              ▼                ▼                ▼                    │
│      ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐             │
│      │ SUBSCRIBER 1 │ │ SUBSCRIBER 2 │ │ SUBSCRIBER 3 │             │
│      │              │ │              │ │              │             │
│      │ LogToFile()  │ │ SendEmail()  │ │ UpdateUI()   │             │
│      └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘             │
│                                                                     │
│  - Subscribers don't know about each other                          │
│  - Publisher doesn't know WHO is listening                          │
│  - Loose coupling!                                                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Basic Event Syntax

```bash
mkdir EventDemo && cd EventDemo
dotnet new console
```

```csharp
// Step 1: Define a delegate type (or use built-in EventHandler)
delegate void ThresholdReachedHandler(string message);

// PUBLISHER class
class Counter
{
    private int _count = 0;
    private int _threshold;

    // Step 2: Declare the EVENT using the delegate type
    public event ThresholdReachedHandler? ThresholdReached;

    public Counter(int threshold)
    {
        _threshold = threshold;
    }

    public void Increment()
    {
        _count++;
        Console.WriteLine($"Count: {_count}");

        if (_count >= _threshold)
        {
            // Step 3: RAISE the event (only the owner can do this)
            ThresholdReached?.Invoke($"Threshold {_threshold} reached!");
        }
    }
}

// SUBSCRIBER class
class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var counter = new Counter(threshold: 3);

        // Step 4: SUBSCRIBE to the event
        counter.ThresholdReached += OnThresholdReached;
        counter.ThresholdReached += msg => Console.WriteLine($"[Lambda] {msg}");

        counter.Increment();  // Count: 1
        counter.Increment();  // Count: 2
        counter.Increment();  // Count: 3  → Events fire!

        // These would cause COMPILE ERRORS:
        // counter.ThresholdReached("fake!");           // ❌ Can't invoke from outside
        // counter.ThresholdReached = OnThresholdReached; // ❌ Can't overwrite with =
    }

    // Event handler method
    static void OnThresholdReached(string message)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"[Handler] {message}");
    }
}
```

Output:
```
Count: 1
Count: 2
Count: 3
[Handler] Threshold 3 reached!
[Lambda] Threshold 3 reached!
```


## Standard .NET Event Pattern

In real-world .NET, events follow a **convention** using `EventHandler` or `EventHandler<TEventArgs>`:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  .NET EVENT CONVENTION                                              │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  delegate void EventHandler(object? sender, EventArgs e);           │
│                                       │            │                │
│                                       │            └─ Event data    │
│                                       └─ Who raised the event       │
│                                                                     │
│  For custom data:                                                   │
│  delegate void EventHandler<TEventArgs>(object? sender, TEventArgs e);│
│                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Example with Custom EventArgs

```csharp
// Custom event data class
class ScanCompletedEventArgs : EventArgs
{
    public string PatientId { get; }
    public string Modality { get; }
    public int ImageCount { get; }
    public DateTime CompletedAt { get; }

    public ScanCompletedEventArgs(string patientId, string modality, int imageCount)
    {
        PatientId = patientId;
        Modality = modality;
        ImageCount = imageCount;
        CompletedAt = DateTime.Now;
    }
}

// PUBLISHER: The scanner
class DicomScanner
{
    // Standard event pattern: EventHandler<TEventArgs>
    public event EventHandler<ScanCompletedEventArgs>? ScanCompleted;
    public event EventHandler<int>? ProgressChanged;  // Simple built-in type

    public void PerformScan(string patientId, string modality, int slices)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"Starting {modality} scan for patient {patientId}...\n");

        for (int i = 1; i <= slices; i++)
        {
            Thread.Sleep(300);  // Simulate scanning

            // Raise progress event
            int percent = i * 100 / slices;
            ProgressChanged?.Invoke(this, percent);
        }

        // Raise completion event with custom data
        var args = new ScanCompletedEventArgs(patientId, modality, slices);
        ScanCompleted?.Invoke(this, args);
    }
}

// SUBSCRIBERS
class NotificationService
{
    public void OnScanCompleted(object? sender, ScanCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"\n📧 Notification: {e.Modality} scan completed");
        Console.WriteLine($"   Patient: {e.PatientId}");
        Console.WriteLine($"   Images: {e.ImageCount}");
        Console.WriteLine($"   Time: {e.CompletedAt:HH:mm:ss}");
    }
}

class AiAnalysisService
{
    public void OnScanCompleted(object? sender, ScanCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"\n🤖 AI Analysis queued for {e.ImageCount} images");
    }
}

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        // Create publisher
        var scanner = new DicomScanner();

        // Create subscribers
        var notifier = new NotificationService();
        var aiService = new AiAnalysisService();

        // Subscribe to events
        scanner.ScanCompleted += notifier.OnScanCompleted;
        scanner.ScanCompleted += aiService.OnScanCompleted;
        scanner.ProgressChanged += (sender, percent) =>
        {
            Console.Write($"\rProgress: {percent}%");
        };

        // Run the scan
        scanner.PerformScan("P-12345", "CT Chest", 5);
    }
}
```

Output:
```
Starting CT scan for patient P-12345...

Progress: 100%
📧 Notification: CT Chest scan completed
   Patient: P-12345
   Images: 5
   Time: 14:32:15

🤖 AI Analysis queued for 5 images
```


## Unsubscribing from Events (Important!)

Always unsubscribe to prevent **memory leaks**:

```csharp
class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        var scanner = new DicomScanner();
        
        // Subscribe
        EventHandler<ScanCompletedEventArgs> handler = OnScanCompleted;
        scanner.ScanCompleted += handler;

        // ... do work ...

        // Unsubscribe when done (important for long-lived publishers!)
        scanner.ScanCompleted -= handler;
    }

    static void OnScanCompleted(object? sender, ScanCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Scan done!");
    }
}
```

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WHY UNSUBSCRIBE?                                                   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  Publisher holds REFERENCES to all subscribers                      │
│                                                                     │
│  If subscriber should be garbage collected but is still             │
│  subscribed → MEMORY LEAK (publisher keeps it alive)                │
│                                                                     │
│  Common in UI apps: Window closes but event handlers remain         │
│                                                                     │
│  Rule: If publisher outlives subscriber → UNSUBSCRIBE!              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Complete Pattern: Protected Virtual Method

The recommended pattern for classes that might be inherited:

```csharp
class DicomScanner
{
    public event EventHandler<ScanCompletedEventArgs>? ScanCompleted;

    // Protected virtual method to raise the event
    // Allows derived classes to override behavior
    protected virtual void OnScanCompleted(ScanCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        ScanCompleted?.Invoke(this, e);
    }

    public void PerformScan(string patientId, string modality, int slices)
    {
        // ... scanning logic ...

        // Use the protected method to raise event
        OnScanCompleted(new ScanCompletedEventArgs(patientId, modality, slices));
    }
}

// Derived class can extend behavior
class AdvancedScanner : DicomScanner
{
    protected override void OnScanCompleted(ScanCompletedEventArgs e)
    {
        Console.WriteLine("Pre-processing before notifying subscribers...");
        base.OnScanCompleted(e);  // Call base to fire the event
        Console.WriteLine("Post-processing after notifying subscribers...");
    }
}
```


## Event Flow Summary

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  EVENT LIFECYCLE                                                    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                     │
│  1. DECLARE event in publisher:                                     │
│     public event EventHandler<MyArgs>? MyEvent;                     │
│                                                                     │
│  2. SUBSCRIBE in consumer:                                          │
│     publisher.MyEvent += MyHandler;                                 │
│                                                                     │
│  3. RAISE event in publisher (when something happens):              │
│     MyEvent?.Invoke(this, new MyArgs(...));                         │
│                                                                     │
│  4. HANDLER executes in subscriber:                                 │
│     void MyHandler(object? sender, MyArgs e) { ... }                │
│                                                                     │
│  5. UNSUBSCRIBE when done:                                          │
│     publisher.MyEvent -= MyHandler;                                 │
│                                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Comparison Summary

| Aspect | Delegate | Event |
|--------|----------|-------|
| External Subscribe (`+=`) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| External Unsubscribe (`-=`) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| External Invoke | ✅ Yes (risky) | ❌ No |
| External Overwrite (`=`) | ✅ Yes (risky) | ❌ No |
| Encapsulation | Low | High |
| Use case | Callbacks, LINQ | Notifications, UI |
